analysis.title: Is a Corporate Tax Rate Hike in the Cards? (Investment Strategy Weekly, November 6, 2026)
key_insights: Democrats regained both the House (at least 253 seats) and the Senate (at least 54 seats, flipping at least seven including Texas, South Carolina and Kansas) and captured several governorships. Market volatility has increased since Election Day.

Data center buildout: new governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia who campaigned on stricter data center rules could make approvals harder. Restrictions generally would not stop projects already underway, so any slowdown is a 2028-and-beyond story. Capacity under construction is about 150% of what is operational today.

If data center construction slows, chipmakers could see weaker demand, while hyperscalers that own existing capacity could benefit from a supply-constrained environment and less balance sheet pressure. The firm is watching the trajectory of AI capex, which accounted for a significant share of economic growth over the past year.
Raymond James remains overweight Technology following the sector's pullback, and says the AI ecosystem can navigate post-election regulatory challenges.

Iran war: markets see the election as lowering escalation risk, reflected in lower oil prices. The firm cautions against calling the conflict resolved because foreign policy remains under White House control, the US and Iran remain far apart, and US forces remain in the region.

The firm's non-consensus 12-month WTI target is $65, based on an Iran off-ramp over the next six months. It stays underweight Energy and favors Consumer Discretionary and Industrials, particularly transports.

Taxes: sweeping tax changes look unlikely until 2029 at the earliest because President Trump retains the veto and an override needs two-thirds of both chambers. A Democratic sweep in 2028 could raise rates on capital gains, dividends, estates, corporate earnings and high-earner ordinary income.

Debt limit: Republicans have about six weeks before Democrats take control and could address it in the lame-duck session, possibly with year-end funding. Failure could make the debt ceiling a major Washington risk in 2027.

The firm expects the 10-year Treasury yield to move toward 4.5%-4.75% over the next 12 months on slowing growth and cooling inflation. Treasury auction bid-to-cover ratios near 2.5x show healthy demand.

Bipartisan compromise: moderate Democrats did well, and the firm sees possible deals on defense spending, health care, energy permitting and clean energy. Compromise could widen the deficit. This supports an overweight to Industrials, while valuations keep Health Care neutral.
October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, above expectations, with August and September revised up by a combined 84,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1% despite higher labor force participation.
Q3 2026 productivity rose 3.6% QoQ, unit labor costs fell 0.7% (first decline since 2Q25), and labor's share of output hit a record low of 53%.
October ISM Manufacturing rose to 55.5, the highest since 2021. ISM Services edged down to 54.5. Both remain in expansion.

Rate hike expectations for the December FOMC meeting have moved up to about 79%. The firm expects headline and core CPI unchanged at 3.7% and 2.6% YoY. CPI is due Tuesday and PPI Friday, the last prints before the meeting.
Equities: since 1942, both chambers flipped after a midterm four times (1946, 1954, 1994, 2006). The S&P 500 gained 17% on average over the following 12 months and was positive in all four cases.

AI divergence: semiconductors are down 14% week to date while hyperscalers are up 2%. Semiconductor valuations relative to the S&P 500 are near their lowest in at least 30 years, and the firm sees healthy demand through at least 2027.
Constellation and NRG report earnings Monday and are the focus for power demand growth assumptions after independent power producers reacted negatively to the election.

The 10-year Treasury yield is down nearly 50 bps from its 5.31% closing peak a month ago to its lowest since Labor Day. Historically, monthly declines of 50 bps or more were followed by an average 5 bps rise the next month (10 bps outside recessions).

Hyperscalers issued about $67B of bonds in one week, bringing 2026 issuance to $296B. Deals included Microsoft $25B, Oracle $10B, Meta about $25B and Alphabet about $6.7B. USD deals were 3.8-4.6x covered. IG spreads rose only 1 bp to 91 bps.

The Bank of England raised its policy rate 25 bps to 4.0%, its first hike since August 2023, so all G7 central banks have hiked at least once in 2026. The UK 10-year yield is 5.20%, the highest in the G7.
Weekly market moves (Nov 5): S&P 500 -4.7%, Nasdaq Composite -7.1%, Information Technology -12.0%, Energy -10.1%, WTI crude -11.3% to $90.5, gold +2.0% to $4113.5.

tension_points.theme: data center regulation and AI capex
tension_points.bull_case: Capacity under construction is about 150% of what is operational, underlying AI demand is robust, and hyperscalers could benefit from supply constraints. Semiconductor valuations are near 30-year lows relative to the S&P 500.
tension_points.bear_case: State restrictions in Texas, Ohio and Georgia could slow approvals and weigh on chipmaker demand, and a meaningful slowdown in AI capex, a large contributor to growth, could be a warning sign.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Political rhetoric at the state level translating into tangible regulatory action, or a meaningful slowdown in AI capex.

tension_points.bull_case: An off-ramp over the next six months supports the $65 12-month WTI target, and an earlier resolution could accelerate oil's decline.
tension_points.bear_case: The US and Iran remain far apart, US forces remain in the region, and the White House controls foreign policy, so geopolitical risk has not disappeared.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report does not name a specific level, but an earlier resolution would accelerate oil's decline and persistent escalation would undermine the $65 target.

theme_stances.key_argument: New restrictions generally would not stop projects already underway, so any slowdown is a 2028-and-beyond story and the AI megatrend is not over.
The Iran conflict ultimately finds an off-ramp over the next six months, supporting a $65 WTI target.
Slowing growth and cooling inflation should pull the 10-year yield toward 4.5%-4.75%.
